Talphera Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update

 

Briefing document submitted to FDA for a Sprint Meeting requesting a close of the NEPHRO CRRT study enrollment based on number of patients enrolled as of December 31, 2026

 

Pivotal NEPHRO study currently exceeds 80% power for primary endpoint supporting a potential early close of enrollment

 

Updated market research raises nafamostat peak sales estimate for CRRT above $200 million

 

Cash and investments of $14.2 million at September 30, 2026

 

Conference call and webcast to be held on Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET

 

SAN MATEO, Calif., November 12, 2026 – Talphera, Inc. (Nasdaq: TLPH) (“Talphera”), a specialty pharmaceutical company developing nafamostat as a regional anticoagulant for use in continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026 and provided a business update. The update covers Talphera’s proposed PMA filing plan for nafamostat and its increased commercial opportunity.

 

“We believe nafamostat has the potential to address an important unmet need as a regional anticoagulant for critically ill patients undergoing CRRT,” stated Vince Angotti, CEO of Talphera. “Our updated market research, including physician feedback on nafamostat compared with currently used products, supports its potential adoption in CRRT and an increased peak sales estimate of more than $200 million.”

 

Vince Angotti continued, “Enrollment in the NEPHRO CRRT study has slowed over recent months, primarily due to fewer qualifying patients at our clinical sites. Enrolling these critically ill patients is challenging and other recent CRRT studies having faced similar difficulties. Some sponsors closed enrollment early and subsequently received regulatory approval.”

 

“To date, we have enrolled more than 75% of the planned 70 patients. To support our goal of completing the study this year, we have submitted a briefing document to the FDA seeking feedback on closing enrollment as of December 31, 2026, even if fewer than the targeted 70 patients are enrolled. While the study remains blinded and open for enrollment, we believe the current enrollment is sufficient to support a PMA filing as it has over 80% statistical power for the primary endpoint,” concluded Vince Angotti.

 

 

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

 

●

Submitted a briefing document to the FDA seeking feedback on a regulatory strategy for a PMA filing based on final NEPHRO CRRT study enrollment as of December 31, 2026, even if fewer than the targeted 70 patients are enrolled.

 

●

Increased estimated peak sales for nafamostat in CRRT to more than $200 million, based on updated qualitative and quantitative market research.

 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Information

 

●

The cash and investments balance was $14.2 million as of September 30, 2026.

 

●

Combined R&D and SG&A expenses for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $4.1 million compared to $3.4 million for the third quarter of 2025. Excluding non-cash stock-based compensation expense, these amounts were $3.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $3.3 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase in combined R&D and SG&A expenses in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to increased Niyad development project activities, and certain SG&A expenses related to pre-launch commercial preparation activities.

 

●

Net loss attributable to common shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $4.0 million, or $0.05 per basic and diluted share, compared to a net loss of $4.4 million, or $0.11 per basic and diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.

 

●

Talphera plans to file a Form S-3 Shelf Registration Statement to replace its existing Form S-3 that expires on November 30, 2026.

About Talphera, Inc.

 

Talphera, Inc. is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative therapies for use in medically supervised settings. Talphera's lead product candidate, Niyad® is a lyophilized formulation of nafamostat and is currently being studied under an investigational device exemption (IDE) as an anticoagulant for the extracorporeal circuit, and has received Breakthrough Device Designation status from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

 

This release is intended for investors only. For additional information about Talphera, please visit www.talphera.com.

 

About Niyad and Nafamostat

 

Nafamostat is a broad spectrum, synthetic serine protease inhibitor with anticoagulant, anti-inflammatory and potential anti-viral activities. Niyad® is a lyophilized formulation of nafamostat and is currently being studied under an IDE, as an anticoagulant for the extracorporeal circuit, and has received Breakthrough Device Designation Status from the FDA. Talphera’s registrational study of Niyad is named the NEPHRO CRRT (Nafamostat Efficacy in Phase 3 Registrational Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy) study. An ICD-10 procedural code, XY0YX37, has been issued for the extracorporeal introduction of nafamostat. The ICD-10 code is a specific/billable code that can be used to indicate a procedure. LTX-608 is a proprietary nafamostat formulation for direct IV infusion that may be investigated and developed for the treatment of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), acute pancreatitis or as an anti-viral treatment, amongst other potential targets.

 

About the NEPHRO CRRT Study

 

The NEPHRO CRRT Study is designed as a prospective, double-blinded trial to be conducted at up to 14 U.S. hospital intensive care units. The study is intended to enroll and evaluate 70 adult patients undergoing renal replacement therapy who cannot tolerate heparin or are at risk for bleeding. The primary endpoint of the study is mean post-filter activated clotting time using Niyad versus placebo over the first 24 hours. The study is powered over 90% for the primary endpoint with 70 patients. Key secondary endpoints include the mean post-filter activated clotting time over 72 hours, filter lifespan, number of filter changes over 72 hours, number of transfusions over 72 hours and dialysis efficacy (based on urea concentration) over the first 24 hours.
